records.title: 2.0L Turbo (LSY) Excessive Oil Consumption and PCV System Failure
records.description: Owners of four-cylinder CT5 550T (and CT4-shared LSY platform) models report higher-than-expected oil consumption, often exceeding GM's 'acceptable' threshold of one quart per ~2,000 miles. The valve-cover-integrated PCV system is a frequent contributor, and on worse cases worn piston rings or turbo seals allow oil into the combustion chamber. Symptoms commonly appear between 40,000 and 80,000 miles and are accompanied by low-oil warnings between changes, a lit check-engine light, and sometimes boost/lean codes. The PCV diaphragm is built into the valve cover, so a failed PCV requires valve-cover replacement rather than a standalone valve on some service variants.
records.solution: Have the dealer run a documented oil-consumption test; consumption beyond GM's spec can qualify for warranty repair. First-line fix is the PCV/valve-cover assembly (ACDelco PCV service part 12714149 applies to LSY CT5 on standalone-valve variants); persistent consumption after PCV service points to a piston-ring or turbo-seal repair under powertrain warranty. Maintain 5,000-mile changes with dexos1 Gen 3 0W-20 to protect the turbo and rings. Out-of-warranty PCV/valve-cover work is modest; a ring/teardown repair is the expensive end.
symptoms: Frequent low-oil level warnings between oil changes
Burning-oil smell or light blue exhaust smoke
Rough idle or hesitation from a vacuum leak
Check engine light with lean or boost-pressure codes

records.title: 10-Speed (10L80/10L90) Transmission Control Valve Wear Causing Momentary Wheel Lock-Up (Recall 25V-148)
records.description: NHTSA Recall 25V-148 covers roughly 27,097 model-year 2020-2021 CT5 vehicles with the GM Hydra-Matic 10-speed automatic. A transmission control valve can wear excessively over time due to an internal fluid leak, gradually losing line pressure. This first shows up as harsh or erratic shifting, and in rare cases can cause a momentary rear-wheel lock-up during a downshift (notably an 8-7 downshift) at speed — a loss-of-control hazard. This is a distinct mechanism from the previously documented line-pressure-solenoid P2812/P2814 fault and the adaptive-learning shift-quality concern.
records.solution: This is a free safety recall. Dealers reprogram the Transmission Control Module with software that detects excessive control-valve wear roughly 10,000 miles before lock-up could occur and limits the transmission to a maximum of fifth gear, preventing the dangerous downshift. Owners should verify the recall against their VIN at the NHTSA site. If wear has already caused damage, valve-body service is required; that work is the high end of the cost range when not covered.
symptoms: Harsh, hard, or clunky gear changes
Momentary rear-wheel lock-up or lurch during deceleration/downshift
Slipping or delayed engagement
Transmission fluid leak

records.title: 10L80 10-Speed Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder at Light Throttle
records.description: The CT5 pairs both its 2.0L turbo and 3.0L twin-turbo engines with a GM 10-speed automatic (10L80/10L90), which can develop a torque converter clutch (TCC) shudder felt as a vibration or 'rumble-strip' shake, typically at light throttle and steady cruise (roughly 25-55 mph) when the converter clutch is applying. The accepted root cause is TCC friction-material shedding and fluid contamination degrading TCC apply. GM issued TSB 22-NA-080 covering 10L80/10L90 TCC shudder (added July 2022, later revised to add newer model years). This is distinct from the 10L80/10L90 control-valve-wear recall and from harsh-shift/solenoid codes. Verified: TSB 22-NA-080 exists and covers this transmission family; CT5 use of the 10-speed with both engines is confirmed; CT5/V-Series owner shudder reports are corroborated on forums.
records.solution: Per TSB 22-NA-080, the fix is a Transmission Control Module (TCM) recalibration combined with a complete transmission fluid exchange to the specified Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP (GM PN 19417577). If shudder persists after the fluid/recalibration service (indicating advanced clutch-material contamination), the torque converter and a full fluid flush/replacement are required.
symptoms: Vibration or shudder at light throttle / steady cruise
'Rumble-strip' shake felt through the vehicle around 25-55 mph
Shudder most noticeable when torque converter clutch engages
Momentary shake that comes and goes under light load

records.title: 10L80 Harsh Shifts and Check Engine Light with DTC P2812 or P2814 (Line Pressure Solenoid)
records.description: Owners of 2020-2021 Cadillac CT5 and CT5-V models equipped with the GM Hydra-Matic 10L80 10-speed automatic report harsh, abrupt shifts accompanied by an illuminated check engine light. GM Preliminary Information bulletin PIP5799 documents an electrical fault in Transmission Control Solenoid Valve 7 (the line pressure solenoid) that stores DTC P2812 or P2814 in the TCM. Separately, NHTSA Safety Recall N242480630 (NHTSA 25V148) covers TCM monitoring software for a related transmission control valve wear condition that, in rare cases, can cause momentary wheel lock-up. A related Special Coverage bulletin (N242480631) extends warranty for the P0747 control-valve condition to 15 years / 150,000 miles. Note: the 2020-2021 CT5 does not include the CT5-V Blackwing (introduced for MY2022 with the 10L90), which is NOT part of this recall population.
records.solution: Scan the TCM; if P2812 or P2814 is set, follow SI diagnostics for the line pressure solenoid circuit. PIP5799 directs that, if no other root cause is found, the valve body is replaced. Also verify GM Safety Recall N242480630 (TCM monitoring software for wheel lock-up risk) has been performed; owner letters were mailed April 7, 2025. If P0747 sets after the TCM update, the control valve body replacement is covered under Special Coverage N242480631 for 15 years / 150,000 miles.
symptoms: Harsh or abrupt shifts
Check engine / SES light
Reduced engine performance / Reduced Propulsion message
Possible momentary wheel lock-up (subject of recall N242480630)

citations.title: PIP5799 — 10L60 10L80 10L90 10L1000 Automatic Transmissions With SES Light And DTCs P2812 Or P2814 Setting

communityRecommendations.content: If you experience harsh shifts, pull codes first — a stored P2812 or P2814 points directly to the line pressure solenoid and qualifies the car for PIP5799 diagnostics under powertrain warranty.

Verify Recall N242480630 has been completed via NHTSA VIN lookup; the TCM monitoring software update is free and addresses a wheel lock-up safety risk. If a P0747 subsequently sets, the control valve body replacement is covered for 15 years / 150,000 miles under Special Coverage N242480631.

records.title: 2.0T LSY Engine Timing Cover Oil Leak
records.description: The 2.0T turbocharged four-cylinder (LSY) in the CT5 can develop oil leaks from the timing cover gasket. The gasket develops cracks after heat cycling, causing oil to seep from the front of the engine. In some cases, this leads to noticeable oil consumption between changes. GM revised the 2.0T engine (LSY) for 2020+ which reduced but did not eliminate the issue. Using incorrect oil viscosity can worsen the problem.
records.solution: Confirm the leak by cleaning the front of the LSY engine, adding UV dye if needed, and inspecting the timing cover perimeter, upper oil pan junctions, and front crankshaft seal area to rule out a valve cover or seal leak. Repair typically requires removing the accessory drive components and front cover, resealing or replacing the timing cover gasket/sealant with updated GM parts, and inspecting the cover for warpage or damage before reassembly to factory torque specs; if oil contamination is heavy, replace the drive belt as well. Finish with an oil and filter change using the correct Dexos-approved viscosity specified by GM and verify no further seepage after a road test. Typical repair cost is about $900-$1,800 depending on labor time and whether the front seal, belt, or related seals are replaced.
symptoms: Oil level dropping between changes
Oil seepage visible at front of engine
Burning oil smell after driving
Low oil level warning light
Oil spots on garage floor under front of vehicle

records.title: Auto Stop/Start Rough Restart with Brake and Stability Warning Lights
records.description: CT5 owners report problems tied to the auto stop/start system: during an auto-restart, multiple warning lights (traction control, electronic brake system/EBS, and brake-related) can illuminate, the car can become hard to steer and slow to brake for a moment, and the engine can shudder or clunk back to life. Forum responses attribute this to a voltage glitch during the restart event and an aging/weak 12V or auxiliary battery, which struggles to support the system through the restart cycle.
records.solution: Have the dealer load-test the 12V battery and charging system — a weak or aged battery is the most common root cause and the system increasingly disables stop/start as the battery degrades. Possible powertrain-warranty coverage applies if warning lights recur. Software updates address some restart glitches. Replacing the battery (and resetting/relearning the battery sensor) typically restores normal stop/start operation; owners who only want to silence the feature can disable it each drive.
symptoms: Engine shudders or clunks on auto-restart
Multiple warning lights (traction/EBS/brake) flash on restart
Momentary heavy steering or weak braking after restart
Auto stop/start stops functioning entirely

records.title: Driver Seat Massage and Lumbar/Bolster Module Failure
records.description: A widely reported CT5 interior failure: the driver-seat massage and adjustable lumbar/bolster functions stop working. Dealers diagnose this as a failed seat 'module' — an all-in-one air-pump, valve and electronics unit feeding the seat air bladders. Owners report the failure from as early as factory delivery up through ~20,000 miles, and some have waited months for the part. Both standard and Recaro/performance seats are affected.
records.solution: The fix is replacement of the seat bolster/massage pump-and-valve module (and occasionally the air bladders or hoses), typically covered under the new-vehicle warranty. Confirm the dealer has GM repair information for the specific seat variant, as parts availability has caused long delays. Out-of-warranty, expect module-plus-labor cost in the listed range.
symptoms: Massage function inoperative
Lumbar or side-bolster adjustment does not move
Audible pump runs but seat does not inflate
No air-bladder response from seat controls

records.title: Daytime Running Lights Won't Turn Off With Headlights (Recall 22V903 / N222386380)
records.description: GM recalled certain 2020-2023 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 (along with 2021-2023 Buick Envision and 2022-2023 Cadillac Escalade/Escalade ESV, Chevrolet Silverado 1500/Suburban/Tahoe, and GMC Sierra 1500/Yukon/Yukon XL — 740,108 vehicles total) because the daytime running lamps may not deactivate when the headlamps are on, failing to comply with FMVSS 108 'Lamps, Reflective Devices, and Associated Equipment.' DRLs that do not deactivate may produce glare, reducing visibility and increasing crash risk. The root cause is a body control module software issue; a GM vehicle controls engineer submitted a report to GM's Speak Up For Safety program on October 6, 2022, after a similar issue was found in 2021 full-size SUVs (recall 22V827), and the investigation expanded into this campaign (22V903). Base trim vehicles that share a single light source for low-beams and DRLs are not affected.
records.solution: The body control module software is updated by a dealer or via an over-the-air (OTA) update, free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed January 23, 2023. Owners may contact Cadillac customer service at 1-800-458-8006 and reference GM recall N222386380 / NHTSA 22V903000. Confirm remedy status by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.
symptoms: Front DRLs remain illuminated when low/high beams active
Oncoming traffic flashes you
Cadillac mobile app or NHTSA VIN check flags an open recall

records.title: Electric Water Pump Circuit Board Failure — Overheat and Limp Mode
records.description:
GM issued a TSB (December 2020) stating the printed circuit board inside the electric water pump on affected CT4/CT5 vehicles may have been manufactured incorrectly, potentially causing a water pump failure; when this occurs the vehicle displays warnings as coolant temperatures rise, the oil pressure gauge falsely indicates high oil pressure, a reduced power/torque message appears, and if ignored the AC is disabled and the driver is told to turn off the engine
. 
The 2.0L LSY turbo-four (base engine in the CT5) is one of the engines susceptible to this water pump failure (the other being the 2.7L L3B, which is not used in the CT5)
.
records.solution:
Dealers inspect and, if necessary, replace the entire water pump assembly; the job takes roughly four hours and was performed at no cost to the owner under the Customer Satisfaction Program TSB
. 
The TSB coverage window ran through December 31, 2022, so out-of-warranty owners now face out-of-pocket cost
. Independent shop cost for the electric pump assembly typically runs $700–$1,400 parts plus labor. Diagnose by scanning for coolant temp DTCs and observing the false-high oil pressure indication, which is a hallmark of this specific failure mode.
symptoms: High coolant temperature warning
Oil pressure gauge falsely reading high
'Reduced engine power' message
AC compressor cut out
'Turn off engine' chime/message
No coolant flow at idle

citations.title: New Service Bulletin Addresses Water Pump Issues On Cadillac CT4, CT5
TSB for CT4 and CT5 water pump failure

communityRecommendations.content: The falsely-high oil pressure reading on a 2.0T LSY almost always indicates electric water pump electronics failure, NOT an oil problem — do not change the oil pump or sender chasing this symptom.
Pull over and shut down immediately when the 'reduced power' / overheat warnings cascade. Continuing to drive past the third warning (engine shutoff request) risks head gasket and turbo damage.

records.title: Electronic Brake Boost Module Failure — Loss of Brake Assist (2020 Recall)
records.description: GM recalled 2020 Cadillac CT4, CT5 and XT4 vehicles because contamination introduced during the supplier's material production process can affect a sensor connection in the electronic brake-boost system. Under certain conditions, communication between the sensor and the brake-boost system can be interrupted, causing a loss of electronic brake assist. The driver must then apply substantially greater pedal force to slow or stop the car, increasing crash risk. This is separate from the upper-intermediate-steering-shaft brake-line chafing concern already documented.
records.solution: Free recall remedy: Cadillac dealers replace the entire electronic brake-booster module. Affected owners should confirm against their VIN; the recall began in November 2020. The OEM power/ABS brake-booster assembly for the CT5 is GM 84906162 (electronic brake-booster control module variant 84779555); a replacement requires programming, so out-of-warranty repairs should be done with GM/dealer tooling.
symptoms: Hard brake pedal requiring much greater foot pressure
Longer stopping distances
Brake system / service brake assist warning message
ABS or traction-control lights

records.title: Gloss Black Exterior Trim (B-Pillar / Window Surround) Peeling and Delamination
records.description: A common cosmetic defect on 2020-2024 CT5 models: the gloss-black exterior B-pillar appliqués and window-surround trim bubble, haze, and delaminate, with the clear top layer lifting and flaking to expose a dull layer beneath. Owners describe small bubbles or a milky look first, progressing to peeling. The root cause is a manufacturing defect in the trim's adhesive/finish layers rather than owner abuse, and it affects multiple body panels around the side glass.
records.solution: While under the new-vehicle/bumper-to-bumper warranty, dealers are aware of the defect and replace the affected trim panels at no cost. Out of warranty, owners replace the appliqué panels, apply a gloss-black vinyl wrap, or fit adhesive covers. Document the defect early and request replacement before warranty expires.
symptoms: Bubbling or milky haze under the gloss-black trim
Clear layer lifting or flaking off
Dull/unfinished patches on B-pillar or window surround
Peeling spreading across adjacent trim

records.title: High-Speed Wind Noise / Whistle from Windshield A-Pillar Weatherstrip
records.description: CT5 owners report a persistent whistle or high-pitched 'tone' (described as ringing in the ears) at highway speeds, typically 65 mph and up, plus buzzing from the door/window/headliner area at 50+ mph. Sources isolated by owners and dealers include the windshield weatherstrip lifting where it splits at the center, gaps in door weatherstripping, and even loose interior door-panel labels/tape flapping in the airstream behind trim.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform a wind-noise diagnosis (taping off the A-pillar/windshield seam and mirror base helps isolate the source). The documented fix where the windshield weatherstrip lifts at the center split is replacement with the updated weatherstrip part. Inspect and reseat/replace door weatherstripping and remove any loose internal labels or tape. Most cases are covered under the new-vehicle warranty.
symptoms: Whistle or high-pitched tone at 65+ mph

records.title: Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC / Driver Information Center) Intermittent Blank Screen After Remote Start
records.description: Owners report the digital Instrument Panel Cluster / Driver Information Center (the gauge/speedometer display) going completely blank for the remainder of an ignition cycle, most commonly on cycles that follow a remote start. GM addressed this in Technical Service Bulletin 21-NA-269, which covers the 2020 Cadillac CT4/CT5. The documented root cause is a software fault: infotainment content sent to the IPC from the radio module is sometimes not fully initialized at startup, leaving the cluster blank until the vehicle is shut off and restarted. This is a separate module and separate failure from the center-stack infotainment freezing issue, because it affects the gauge cluster (IPC) and is tied to the startup/remote-start initialization sequence. Verified: the TSB, root cause, and remote-start correlation are corroborated by the GM bulletin summary (oemdtc) and multiple owner reports.
records.solution: Dealer reprograms the Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC) with the latest software calibration per TSB 21-NA-269; no hardware replacement is required in the documented cases. If the cluster fails to respond to reprogramming, the IPC itself may need replacement (and must be programmed to the VIN via GM SPS).
symptoms: Gauge cluster / speedometer display goes completely blank
Blank cluster occurs after using remote start
Display stays blank for the entire drive until the car is restarted
No speed, fuel, or warning information shown

records.title: Performance and Carbon-Ceramic Brake Squeal and Grinding Noise
records.description: CT5 and CT5-V owners (and especially CT5-V Blackwing buyers with the optional Brembo carbon-ceramic package) report loud brake squeal, and at low speed a grindy or metal-on-metal sound, sometimes as early as ~5,000 miles. The copper-free friction-material formulation now mandated, combined with the aggressive performance pad compounds, makes the brakes noisy particularly in warm weather and at low speed. This is a comfort/noise issue rather than a stopping-performance defect, but Blackwing carbon-ceramic rotor replacement is extremely expensive if components are damaged.
records.solution: Verify pad and rotor wear and that no wheel cleaner has been used on carbon-ceramic discs (wheel cleaners degrade the carbon fibers). Re-bedding the pads or switching to a quieter aftermarket compound resolves most cases — owners report PowerStop carbon-ceramic pads (Z26-1405 front / 1053 rear-equivalent) eliminate the squeal and reduce dust on iron-rotor cars. Anti-squeal shims/lubricant on pad backing plates help. Avoid spraying any wheel/brake cleaner near carbon-ceramic rotors.
symptoms: Loud brake squeal, worse above ~50F ambient
Low-speed grinding or metal-on-metal sound
Squeal when pulling away from a stop
Heavy brake dust

records.title: Premature 12V Battery Drain / Parasitic Draw (Memory Seat Module)
records.description: Owners report the 12V battery going dead when the car sits, with factory batteries dying in as little as two years. Beyond normal high parasitic draw of modern electronics, a recurring GM culprit is the driver-seat control module / Memory Seat Module (MSM), which can develop a several-amp draw that flattens the battery overnight; GM has revised these modules multiple times. Audio/amp circuits, the BCM, and sticking door/window switches are other documented draw sources on GM platforms.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic-draw test: with everything asleep, pull fuses one at a time to isolate the offending circuit. If the seat-control/Memory Seat Module is drawing current, replace it with the latest GM-revised part. Confirm the battery itself still holds charge (replace AGM battery if degraded) and check for sticking door/window switches keeping modules awake. A correct battery and an updated MSM resolve most cases.
symptoms: Dead or weak 12V battery after sitting overnight or a few days
Slow crank or no-start
Battery-saver / electrical warnings on startup
Repeated jump-starts needed

records.title: Upper Intermediate Steering Shaft Chafes Front Brake Line (Service Update N202296840)
records.description:
In certain 2020 Cadillac CT5 models the upper intermediate steering shaft can come in contact with the front brake fluid lines and chafe against them; if contact occurs it can cause wear or damage to the fluid lines
. 
This chafing can wear through the brake line, causing a loss of brake fluid and reduced braking performance
. Owners may notice no symptoms until brake fluid loss is severe.
records.solution:
Cadillac dealers inspect the front brake lines and replace them if necessary, along with adjacent parts including front lower control arm bolts, various AC compressor seals, and an engine mount bolt; the service bulletin (N202296840, issued January 2021) is performed when the customer vehicle returns to the dealership for any reason and only affects 2020 model year CT5s
. 
The bulletin expires at the end of the New Vehicle Limited Warranty period
. Owners should request the inspection at any service visit and document brake-pedal feel before/after.
symptoms: Visual chafing/wear marks on front brake line near steering shaft
Brake fluid weeping at line
Low brake fluid warning
Soft brake pedal if line ruptures
No symptom until severe — often found only on inspection

citations.title: 2020 Cadillac CT5 Gets Service Bulletin Over Steering Shaft Issue
2020 Cadillac CT5 TSBs

communityRecommendations.content: Even if your 2020 CT5 has no symptoms, ask the dealer to perform the N202296840 inspection at the next service — it is a no-charge campaign while still within New Vehicle Limited Warranty.

This bulletin is technically a 'service update' rather than a NHTSA safety recall, so it will NOT show up on the standard VIN recall lookup. Ask the dealer to query GM Global Connect for open field actions on the VIN.

records.title: Sunroof / Headliner Rattle and Creak
records.description: Owners of sunroof-equipped CT5 models report creaking and rattling from the roof/sunroof and headliner area, especially over bumps and at speed. GM has a related sunroof-creak service bulletin (TSB 19-NA-096) that calls for dropping the headliner and torquing the sunroof module bolts to spec. Forum members also trace noise to plastic-to-plastic contact at the sunroof trim ring and to loose interior trim near the headliner.
records.solution: For a creak, the dealer follows TSB 19-NA-096 — lower the headliner and re-torque the sunroof bolts to specification. DIY owners report success applying felt/anti-squeak tape at plastic-to-plastic contact points around the sunroof trim ring and securing loose headliner trim. Confirm sunroof drains are clear to rule out a leak being mistaken for a rattle. Typically covered under warranty.

records.title: Super Cruise 'Unavailable' Message — System Inoperative from Delivery
records.description:

records.title: 10-Speed Transmission Adaptive Learning and Shift Quality
records.description: The CT5 uses GM's 10-speed automatic (10L80) that can exhibit harsh shifts, delayed engagement, and shift hunting, particularly when the adaptive learning resets. The 10-speed has very complex shift logic and can take 500+ miles to fully adapt to a driver's pattern after a battery disconnect, TCM update, or reset. Some CT5 owners report persistent shift quality issues even after adaptation. The CT5-V and CT5-V Blackwing have refined calibrations but can still exhibit occasional harsh shifts.
records.solution: Have dealer perform latest TCM software calibration - GM releases regular updates. Allow 500+ miles after any reset for the transmission to relearn. For persistent issues, a full transmission fluid exchange with Mobil 1 LV ATF HP can improve shift quality. Very few CT5s require hardware repair.
symptoms: Harsh 1-2 or 3-4 shifts
Delayed shift from Park to Drive/Reverse
Transmission hunting between gears on hills
Shift quality changes after battery disconnect or service
Clunky low-speed maneuvers

records.title: Infotainment / Center Display Freezing, Black Screen and Stalled Software Update (stuck at 99%)
records.description: CT5 owners report the center infotainment display freezing, becoming unresponsive to touch, or hanging during an over-the-air or dealer-pushed software update — a common symptom is a black screen with a blue progress bar stuck at 99%. The condition is documented on a 2020 CT5 case where a Cadillac-issued Technical Service Bulletin was required to be applied at the dealer to recover the module. Secondary symptoms include incorrect clock display on the instrument cluster after the screen recovers, indicating a system-wide software fault rather than a touchscreen hardware failure. Note: 2020-2024 CT5 uses the pre-Google GM infotainment platform; the CT5 only received Google built-in starting with the 2025 model year, and the reboot procedure differs between the two generations.
records.solution: Try a soft reset first. On 2020-2024 CT5 (pre-Google infotainment): press and hold the infotainment power button (left of the touchscreen) for ~10 seconds until the Cadillac logo reappears. On 2025+ CT5 (Google built-in): with the vehicle in Park, press and hold the steering-wheel phone hang-up button for 10-15 seconds; ignore the on-screen options and the system will reboot in ~5 seconds. If the unit remains stuck (especially at 99% during an update), the fix must be performed at a Cadillac dealer per the active Cadillac TSB, which reflashes the infotainment module. Avoid interrupting any software update by shutting the car off mid-flash — that is the most common trigger for the stuck-update state. A weak 12V battery can also corrupt updates, so have battery state-of-health checked before any reflash.
symptoms: Touchscreen unresponsive or frozen
Black screen with blue progress bar stuck at 99%
Cadillac logo loop on startup
Clock on cluster shows wrong time after recovery
CarPlay/Android Auto won't connect

citations.title: How To Reset Your Cadillac CUE System — Fairfield Cadillac (covers CT5 V-Series)

communityRecommendations.content: If the screen is mid-update, do NOT shut the engine off — let the update complete (5-15 minutes). Interrupting the flash is the #1 cause of the stuck-at-99% state.
Have battery state-of-health tested before any dealer-pushed reflash; a weak 12V battery can corrupt the update and create exactly the freeze symptom the bulletin addresses.

records.title: Tremec 6-Speed Manual 2nd Gear Notchiness and Difficulty
records.description: CT5-V Blackwing models equipped with the Tremec TR-6060 6-speed manual transmission frequently exhibit difficulty and notchiness when shifting into 2nd gear. The issue occurs both when cold and when hot, particularly when downshifting from highway speeds. Some dealers have attributed this to worn synchros requiring complete transmission replacement, while others consider a degree of notchiness normal for the Tremec unit. The problem varies in severity from mildly annoying to preventing clean shifts.
records.solution: Allow the transmission to warm up before aggressive shifting. Use GM-recommended Tremec fluid (Pennzoil Synchromesh) and ensure correct fill level. Rev-matching downshifts can reduce synchro wear. If shifting becomes truly difficult or grinding occurs, have the synchros inspected under warranty. Some owners report improvement after the first 5,000 miles of break-in.
symptoms: Difficulty shifting into 2nd gear when cold
Notchy or resistant feel when selecting 2nd gear
Grinding sensation when downshifting to 2nd at speed
Shift quality degrades in hot weather or after hard driving

records.title: LT4 Supercharged V8 Premature Engine Failure
records.description: The 6.2L supercharged LT4 V8 in CT5-V Blackwing models has experienced premature engine failures including bottom-end bearing failures, lifter collapse, and metal shavings found in oil. Failures have been reported as early as 5,000-15,000 miles. Car and Driver documented a catastrophic engine failure on their long-term test CT5-V Blackwing. GM initially claimed it was an isolated incident but forum reports suggest the problem is more widespread than acknowledged.

If metal is found, stop driving immediately and contact dealer for warranty engine replacement. Keep all service records for warranty claims.
